entity_name: Oregon Residential Specialty Code Table R301.2 (Frost Depth by Elevation)
canonical_name: ORSC Table R301.2 — Frost Line Depth by Elevation
notes: VERIFIED via two independent secondary sources (footingdepth.com + WebSearch AI summary of the ICC/UpCodes table) that were consistent with each other, though the raw ICC table itself could not be directly fetched (403 blocked) this session — flag for direct confirmation against a purchased/library copy of the 2023 ORSC before publishing as a litigation-proof exact figure, consistent with this project's no-fabrication rule. Cited figures: below 2,500 ft elevation = 12 inches; 2,500–4,000 ft = 18 inches; at/above 4,000 ft = 24 inches. Eugene sits at roughly 430 ft elevation and all of Lane County's populated valley floor is well under 2,500 ft, so the 12-inch band governs — meaning Lane County's frost-depth figure and its general minimum-footing-depth figure (R403.1.4) are numerically the same 12 inches, a genuinely simple, quotable fact

entity_name: Oregon Residential Specialty Code R405 (Foundation Drain)
co_occurrence_status: 0/10 competitors mention a code-mandated foundation drain
notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-09: drains are required around concrete/masonry foundations that retain earth and enclose habitable/usable space (basements, habitable crawlspaces), UNLESS the foundation sits on well-drained ground or a sand-gravel-mixture soil. Gravel/crushed-stone footing drains must extend not less than 1 ft beyond the outside edge of the footing and 6 in above the top of the footing, covered with an approved filter membrane; drain tile/perforated pipe sits on 2 in of washed gravel and is covered with 6 in more of the same material. This is the FOUNDATION drain — distinct from the septic drainfield entity (../septic/entity-inventory.csv) and from the yard-scale swale/French-drain entities (../grading-leveling/entity-inventory.csv) — do not conflate the three in content or schema

Directly relevant to an ADU or addition foundation dug near an existing house — a genuine safety/liability fact zero competitors raise

VERIFIED DIRECTLY 2026-09-09 against Eugene's own Inspections page and corroborated by a Lane County-specific inspection-sequence source: the building department's foundation/footing inspection happens AFTER trenches or pad areas are excavated and cleared of loose material or mud, forms are erected and secured, and reinforcing (rebar) is placed and secured — and BEFORE any concrete is poured. In Eugene, inspections are scheduled through eBuild (online) or by calling Inspection Support at 541-682-5283 (7:30am–3:30pm weekdays; request before 7am for same-day). Lane County's own sequence additionally notes the UFER grounding electrode is generally tagged at this same inspection, ahead of the pour. THE single most load-bearing sequencing fact for this page: excavate → inspect → pour, never excavate → pour
